text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000146's elevated 99215 billing appears in every complexity tier, including low-complexity patients, but too few charts were reviewed to confirm or rule out upcoding.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The 99215 share runs several times the all-provider rate in every complexity tier, including patients with zero conditions, and the overall mix sits heavily at 99214. That pattern looks more like a uniform upward billing habit than a sicker panel, though sicker patients do draw more 99215s here. The documentation does not settle it: none of the 5 documented 99215 claims fell below the billed level, but that sample is too small to judge. Two of the supported 99215s, C0073123 (age 20, no chronic conditions, R10.9) and C0073255 (hyperlipidemia only), are low-complexity visits documented at high MDM, and C0073123 also appears among the note-signal examples for problems and data. That is weak evidence the note may be inflated to match the bill, not proof. A reviewer should first request more charts for the low-complexity 99215 claims listed (such as C0072822, C0072892, C0073090 and C0073319), compare their notes for cloned or templated MDM language given the repeated-time signal, and obtain the missing audit trail."}
